summary: Quality management domain foundation adds inspection-plan approval, inspection-lot usage-decision metadata, quality-certificate preparation metadata, quality-notification opening, and SAP QM parity-map linkage while explicitly refusing durable persistence, live inspection runtime, inventory mutation, certificate rendering, CAPA Workflow execution, supplier-network integration, cloud deployment, and runtime audit-chain claims.
non_claims: no inventory blocking or release mutation

findings: The slice is additive and isolates quality-management domain invariants in a flat microservice crate rather than broadening Enterprise Suite into a monolith.
The public API is pure data-in/data-out with no I/O, durable state, network clients, or runtime side effects.
Independent scaling and deployment remain future adapter/runtime work; this slice only creates the pure domain foundation.

F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Tests fail if missing plan approval, inconsistent inspection totals, certificate preparation on rejected lots, notification opening on accepted lots, invalid AQL, invalid dates, unsafe refs, or credential-shaped evidence refs are accepted.
findings: Positive quality flow and negative guard rails are covered.
Types map to inspection plans, inspection lots, usage decisions, certificates, and quality notifications common to ERP quality-management systems.

Focused quality-management tests/clippy, ERP parity map tests/clippy, 30-package enterprise regression tests/clippy, fmt, JSON parse, data_class scan, quality-marker scan, and dependency-seam gate are recorded in verification.

alternatives_named: leave quality management as a parity gap
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: A flat domain foundation gives ERP QM parity a service-owned first write path while keeping inspection runtime, inventory mutation, certificate rendering, CAPA Workflow, supplier collaboration, durable state, and cloud adapters out of scope.
rejected_reasons: Leaving QM as a gap weakens ERP parity after PP, warehouse, procurement, and treasury foundations landed.
Live quality execution and CAPA runtime require durable state, Workflow integration, equipment or lab integrations, inventory semantics, and operational SLO evidence beyond this slice.

findings: No credentials, external network calls, supplier portals, inventory/accounting mutations, or Workflow dispatches are introduced.
Source and audit refs reject traversal, whitespace/control, and credential-shaped strings.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: Pure string/date/quantity validation and small arithmetic only; no I/O or unbounded data access exists.

findings.summary: No database, network, filesystem, equipment integration, scheduler runtime, or hot runtime path is introduced.

data_class_touched: FINANCIAL characteristic/sample/inspection/defect quantities and AQL limits
findings: SAP/Oracle/Microsoft official materials inform quality-management coverage only; no exhaustive vendor parity or proprietary behavior clone is claimed.
The change is additive: one new crate/spec/catalog row and parity-map references; no migration or external resource is introduced.
Static evidence, task rows, and audit-chain rows document the change; runtime audit emission remains a non-claim.
No production user or data migration exists.
Package name follows oya-quality-management-domain and flat microservice layout.
Machine-readable quality-management spec and existing task ledger capture the slice without creating root markdown sprawl.
New code is isolated to microservices/quality-management plus Enterprise Suite parity map references.
Clean architecture is preserved: domain crate depends only on data boundary kernel and std.
No new third-party dependencies were added; Cargo.lock changed only for the new workspace package.
specs/microservices/quality-management.json parses successfully and evidence follows prior multispectrum shape.
AQL max-rejection calculation, pass/fail usage decision, certificate gating, and notification gating are deterministic arithmetic/boolean validation with no hidden state.

M1_challenge_assumption.challenge: A QM row in the parity map could remain a planned gap until runtime integration exists.
M1_challenge_assumption.resolution: The additive domain foundation is lower risk than a runtime claim and establishes a service-owned boundary for future adapters.

M2_independent_review.review_summary: Self-review found no security, architecture, or quality blockers; only known full-verify blockers are unrelated pre-existing catalog/data-class lanes.
